# Everychat Managed — v1 Blueprint

*Generated by idea-forge process, 2026-05-01. Source-of-truth for v1 build.*

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Problem.** EU companies — especially DACH Mittelstand — want LLM chatbots on their websites that are brand-customized, lead-capturing, and DSGVO-compliant. Existing options are either US-headquartered SaaS with sovereignty risk (Intercom Fin, Drift, Chatbase) or custom builds that take months. The only EU-native incumbent is moinAI (Hamburg, since 2015), but they are intent-classification-rooted and slow to LLM-native.

**Chosen approach — "Everychat Managed".** Single-tenant binary architecture (one VM per customer, not multi-tenant SaaS) sold as a managed-hosted service on Everychat-operated Hetzner Cloud at €149/mo, with self-host as an opt-in escape hatch for the ~20% of customers whose IT/legal demands it (€1,500 license + €99/mo support). The build pipeline, eval harness, and `bot-knowledge.bin` format ship under MIT — the commercial product is the managed runtime and the curated **DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus**.

**Why this won.** Phase 1 critique killed the original multi-tenant SaaS on solo-founder capacity grounds (~25% of brief shippable in 6 months) and broken €19 unit economics (Claude Haiku tokens alone exceed the tier price at the chat cap). Phase 2 advanced a self-hosted appliance (B) and edge-only browser-native (D); Phase 3 stress-test killed D on mobile-WebGPU reality and Phi-3-mini German quality, and reframed B from "appliance-first" to "managed-first" because selling Docker tarballs to DACH Mittelstand fails at the Systemhaus interface ("wo ist die .exe?"). The B+D hybrid was rejected as a solo-founder trap.

**The single biggest risk.** First-impression German output quality. Bot embarrasses the Geschäftsführer on first try → churn in week 2. Architecture cannot fix this. **Mitigation: a curated DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus** built from real customer KBs in the first 60 days, used as both eval seed and few-shot prompt material. This is the long-term moat moinAI cannot easily clone.

**6-month v1 success criteria.**
- 10 paying managed-tier customers in production
- Founder downtime ≤ 4h per week on ops
- Bot publish gate: 90%+ pass rate on industry-relevant golden questions before customer first sees the bot
- Zero confirmed cross-customer data exposure
- Public open-source CLI + eval-harness repo with at least 3 external contributors
- 1 self-hosted (€1,500 license) customer signed as proof of the escape hatch

## 2. Concepts Explored

| Concept | One-line description | Why considered | Outcome | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Multi-tenant SaaS** | Next.js + Postgres+pgvector + schema-per-tenant; original brief | User's starting design | **Rejected (v1)** | Solo-team capacity (~25% deliverable in 6mo); multi-tenancy is largest DSGVO risk surface (cross-tenant erasure cascades, shared Ollama leak); €19 unit economics broken; no wedge against moinAI. Reconsider as v2 evolution from B once reference base exists. |
| **B — Self-hosted appliance** | `curl \| bash` Docker appliance on customer VPS; SQLite+sqlite-vec; single Go binary | Phase 1 Architect concept | **Selected (architecture)** | Right architecture (single-tenant binary, structurally trivial DSGVO, no cross-tenant bugs possible). Wrong original go-to-market — Mittelstand IT-Dienstleister won't operate Docker. Reframed as managed-first (see chosen approach). |
| **C — Headless RAG API** | "Algolia of EU sovereignty" — API + multi-frontend reference clients | Phase 1 Architect concept | **Rejected** | 130–150% of A's already-infeasible scope; SMBs don't buy APIs (no v1 buyer); dev-tool GTM ramp misses 12–18 month market window. Reconsider only after 1000+ paying customers on B exist. |
| **D — Edge-only browser-native** | WebLLM + transformers.js in visitor's browser; signed knowledge blob; no backend on runtime path | Phase 1 Architect concept (radical) | **Rejected** | Mobile WebGPU adoption (~30% on iOS Safari) silently fails for B2C; Phi-3-mini German tokenization is below DACH quality bar; 1.4GB cold-load creates customer CDN bills; TTDSG §25 risk on client-side model loads; Mistral could ship `mistral.js` and erase the moat. |
| **E — Hybrid SaaS + Sovereign tier** | Multi-tenant SaaS for €19/€49 + €299 sovereign tier emitting client-side widgets | Phase 1 Architect cross-cut insight | **Parked (v2 north star)** | Strategically attractive (highest optionality, blended margin, clean enterprise pitch) but ~120% of A's already-impossible scope guarantees solo founder ships neither path well. Preserved as year-2 roadmap. |
| **B+D hybrid** | Single binary that can also emit static knowledge blob | Phase 2 Evaluator flagged | **Rejected** | Doubles maintenance and support training; pricing-page confusion drives bounce; solo-founder cognitive-load wall; moinAI weaponizes indecision in sales calls. |
| **Everychat Managed** *(chosen)* | B's single-tenant binary architecture + managed-hosted SaaS go-to-market + open-source build CLI + curated eval corpus | Phase 3 Devil's Advocate synthesis | **Selected** | Solves capacity (single-tenant simplicity, no migration tooling); solves DSGVO (per-customer isolation); solves moat (DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus + community-contributed evals); solves go-to-market (managed default, self-host as opt-in escape); solves sub-processor procurement (Llama Guard from day one, Mistral self-select tier). |

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 Per-customer runtime (one Hetzner VM per customer)

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Customer instance — bot.acme-co.de          │
                    │  Hetzner CCX13 / CCX23 (Ubuntu 24.04)        │

                    │   └────┬─────┘                               │
                    │        │                                     │
                    │        ▼                                     │
                    │   ┌────────────────────────────────────┐     │
                    │   │  everychat-bin  (single Go binary) │     │
                    │   │                                    │     │
```

### 3.2 Operations control plane (founder-side, multi-customer)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Everychat Operations (one Hetzner VM, founder-only)    │
│                                                         │
│  • everychat-ops binary                                 │
│  • Provisioning: Hetzner Cloud API → spin customer VM   │
│  • Deploys: pull latest everychat-bin, restart          │
│  • Telemetry (opt-in only): liveness, version, version  │
│    drift report — NEVER chat content                    │
│  • Mollie webhook receiver — subscription state         │
│  • Postmark — transactional emails (magic link, alerts) │
│  • Backup orchestration → Hetzner Object Storage (EU)   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 3.3 Build pipeline (open-source, MIT)

```
$ npx @everychat/build init
$ npx @everychat/build crawl https://acme-co.de
$ npx @everychat/build ingest ./docs/*.md
$ npx @everychat/build prompt   # generates draft system prompt, opens editor
$ npx @everychat/build eval     # runs golden-questions YAML, exits non-zero on regression
$ npx @everychat/build pack     # emits bot-knowledge.bin + bot-config.json
$ npx @everychat/build push     # deploys to managed instance OR exports for self-host
```

### 3.4 Component inventory

| Component | Tech | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `everychat-bin` | Go 1.22 (single binary, ~30MB) | Chat handler, RAG, admin UI, embed server, lead handler |
| Admin UI | HTMX + AlpineJS embedded in binary | Owner dashboard, no Node runtime needed |
| Storage | SQLite 3.45 + sqlite-vec | Chats, KB chunks, embeddings (Business+ tier), config, leads |
| TLS / reverse proxy | Caddy 2.8 | Auto Let's Encrypt for `bot.<customer-domain>.de` |
| Cloud LLM gateway | LiteLLM (Python sidecar) | Anthropic / Mistral / OpenAI unified interface, cost tracking |
| Local inference | llama.cpp + Mistral-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M | Self-hosted-only path, "no external LLM" tier |
| Moderation | Llama Guard 3 8B (CPU quantized) | Input + output classification, day one |
| Embed widget | iframe panel + light Web Component launcher | `<everychat-launcher>` triggers iframe; iframe is the actual chat UI |
| Auth | Magic link via Postmark | v1: only auth method |
| Billing | Mollie subscriptions | Fixed tiers; no proration / metering at v1 |
| Backup | Restic → Hetzner Object Storage EU | Nightly Postgres-equivalent SQLite snapshots, encrypted |
| Build CLI | `@everychat/build` (Node + TypeScript, MIT) | Crawl, ingest, eval, pack, push |

### 3.5 Data flow — visitor message

```
1. Visitor types in iframe widget
2. POST /api/chat (SSE) with session cookie
3. Llama Guard 3 input check (block if unsafe)
4. KB retrieval:
   - Tier Starter/Pro: full KB stuffed into system prompt + Anthropic prompt cache
   - Tier Business+: sqlite-vec hybrid (BM25 + vector) retrieval + rerank
5. LiteLLM → Anthropic (default) or Mistral (sovereign tier) or local Mistral (self-host)
6. Stream tokens back to widget
7. Llama Guard 3 output check on full response
8. Persist chat turn in SQLite (subject to retention policy)
9. If bot decided "lead handoff" tool → trigger /api/lead flow async
```

### 3.6 Data flow — lead capture

```
1. Bot detects intent or visitor clicks "Connect with Sales"
2. Generate 3-5 line summary via cheap model call
3. Show artifact card in widget: contact name + "Open Email" button
4. mailto: with tokenized transcript link (URL ≤ 1500 chars body)
   OR platform-sent transactional email via Postmark (owner toggle)
5. Async POST to HubSpot Forms API (handle 50 req/10s rate limit with retry queue)
6. Async POST to owner-configured webhook (with SSRF guard: no private IPs, no metadata endpoints)
7. Persist lead in SQLite, surface in admin dashboard
```

### 3.7 Integration points

- **Anthropic Claude** (EU endpoint) — default LLM at Starter / Pro tiers
- **Mistral La Plateforme** (Paris) — opt-in "EU-sovereign" tier
- **Self-hosted Mistral** via llama.cpp — self-host-only / highest-compliance
- **HubSpot Forms API** — lead capture, no OAuth required
- **HubSpot CRM API** (OAuth) — optional transcript-attach, deferred to v1.1
- **Mollie** — subscription billing, fixed tiers
- **Postmark** — transactional email (magic link, lead notifications)
- **Hetzner Cloud API** — VM provisioning for managed instances
- **Hetzner Object Storage (EU)** — backups, signed knowledge blob storage

## 4. Implementation Roadmap (24 weeks)

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation
**Goal:** founder can spin up an empty bot on a Hetzner VM via dashboard.

**Build:**
- `cmd/everychat/` — Go binary skeleton with embedded HTMX admin UI
- `internal/storage/sqlite.go` — schema for `tenants`, `chats`, `messages`, `kb_chunks`, `leads`, `config`
- `internal/auth/magiclink.go` — Postmark integration, signed token
- `Caddyfile` — reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt template
- `cmd/everychat-ops/` — provisioning binary (Hetzner Cloud API)
- `docker-compose.yml` for local dev

**Validation:** `everychat-ops provision --domain bot.test.local --owner-email me@me.de` produces a running instance accessible via magic-link login. Empty admin shows "Create your first bot."

**Complexity:** L. Caddy ACME edge cases and magic-link token rotation under load are foundational risks.

**Not in this phase:** RAG, LLM calls, embed widget, billing.

---

### Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Bot authoring core
**Goal:** founder can build a bot end-to-end and pass golden-questions before publish.

**Build:**
- `internal/crawler/` — domain crawler (homepage, /about, /pricing, /faq, sitemap.xml fallback)
- `internal/ingest/markdown.go` — MD upload → cleaned chunks
- `internal/prompt/generator.go` — LLM-drafted system prompt with editable surface
- `internal/eval/` — golden-questions YAML format, runner, pass/fail report
- LiteLLM Python sidecar in `internal/llm/litellm/`
- Admin UI: bot create wizard, prompt editor, test sandbox, golden-questions editor
- `everychat eval --bot=<id>` CLI command (subset of public CLI)
- **Hard publish gate:** bot cannot go to "live" until evals pass + privacy policy URL + AGB URL set

**Validation:** Build a bot for a fictional Steuerkanzlei. Pass 12/15 golden questions. Publish gate blocks until 14/15.

**Complexity:** L. Eval design quality determines whole product success — invest disproportionately here.

**Not in this phase:** Real visitor traffic, embed code on customer site.

---

### Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Embed + lead capture + DSGVO baseline
**Goal:** dogfood on 1 real customer's website.

**Build:**
- `web/widget/` — TypeScript iframe widget + `<everychat-launcher>` Web Component
- `internal/api/chat.go` — SSE streaming chat endpoint
- `internal/moderation/` — Llama Guard 3 8B integration (CPU quant for Phase 3, GPU later)
- `internal/lead/` — mailto generator + tokenized transcript links + Postmark transactional path
- `internal/integrations/hubspot.go` — Forms API submitter with retry queue (handles 50 req/10s)
- `internal/integrations/webhook.go` — webhook delivery with SSRF guard (private-IP filter, DNS rebind protection, no-redirect)
- DSGVO module: privacy policy URL hard-block, retention scheduler, right-to-erasure cascade (chats + messages + embeddings + leads + audit log)
- Markdown rendering with HTML sanitizer (DOMPurify in widget, server-side validation as backstop)

**Validation:** real customer dogfood — bot lives on a partner Webflow site for 2 weeks, captures ≥10 real leads, no XSS / SSRF / data-leak findings from manual pen-test.

**Complexity:** L. Security-sensitive: this is where most attacks land if v1 fails.

**Not in this phase:** Multi-customer ops, billing, languages other than DE/EN.

---

### Phase 4 (Weeks 13–16): DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus *(the moat)*
**Goal:** bots built from the corpus pass 90% of unseen industry-relevant questions.

**Build:**
- `corpus/` directory with golden-question YAML per industry:
  - `corpus/de/steuerberater/`
  - `corpus/de/maschinenbau/`
  - `corpus/de/versicherung/`
  - `corpus/de/anwaltskanzlei/`
  - `corpus/de/handwerk/`
  - `corpus/de/saas-b2b/`
- `internal/corpus/loader.go` — corpus selection by industry tag in onboarding
- `internal/prompt/fewshot.go` — few-shot prompt assembly using industry exemplars
- Onboarding flow: industry picker → corpus auto-loaded as eval seed
- "Hold-out" question set per industry: 50 unseen questions, target 90% pass rate
- Recruit 4–6 design-partner customers (real DACH SMBs) to contribute KB material under anonymization

**Validation:** Build a bot for design-partner #5 using their KB + corpus few-shot. Without seeing the hold-out questions, the bot scores ≥90% via blind evaluation by partner's Geschäftsführer.

**Complexity:** L (mostly human work — corpus curation is the bottleneck).

**Not in this phase:** Production scaling, public launch.

---

### Phase 5 (Weeks 17–20): Production hardening
**Goal:** 5 paying customers in production with founder downtime ≤ 4h / week.

**Build:**
- `cmd/everychat-ops/` extended: multi-customer provisioning, deploy automation, telemetry (opt-in: version + healthz only — never chat content)
- Mollie subscription integration: signup flow, webhook handler, dunning notifications (manual retry, no auto-retry per Mollie limits)
- Backup automation: Restic → Hetzner Object Storage, daily, encrypted, 30-day retention
- Monitoring: per-customer healthz aggregation, alert routing (Healthchecks.io or PagerDuty Free)
- Llama Guard 3 8B GPU inference path (if Yorizon GPU SKUs land in Q3) or remain on CPU-quant
- Cost dashboard per customer (token usage, monthly projection, alerts)

**Validation:** 5 paying customers running 14 days with no founder-touch incidents. Backup restore drill: restore a customer's instance from yesterday's snapshot in <30 min.

**Complexity:** M. Mostly ops automation, lower technical risk than Phase 2–4.

**Not in this phase:** Open-source release.

---

### Phase 6 (Weeks 21–24): Open-source CLI + go-live
**Goal:** 10 paying customers; public open-source CLI repo with external contributors.

**Build:**
- Extract `cmd/everychat-build/` (CLI) and `internal/eval/` and `format/bot-knowledge/` into separate repo: `github.com/everychat/build`
- MIT license on extracted code
- Documentation site (Docusaurus) at docs.everychat.eu
- Public landing page (everychat.eu) with pricing: Free CLI / €149 Managed / €1,500 Self-host
- Public launch: HN, Product Hunt, German tech press (heise, t3n)
- Self-hosted SKU: licensing server (`license.everychat.eu` issuing JWT tokens with weekly check-in)

**Validation:** 10 paying customers; ≥3 external PRs merged on the open-source CLI repo within 30 days of launch.

**Complexity:** M. Mostly polish and packaging.

**Not in this phase:** Static-export mode, additional languages, native HubSpot OAuth connector.

## 5. Test Specifications

### 5.1 Eval harness (the production-quality gate)

**Format:** YAML per bot:
```yaml
golden_questions:
  - q: "Welche Leistungen bieten Sie für GmbHs an?"
    expected_themes: [steuerberatung, jahresabschluss, lohnabrechnung]
    must_not_say: [fee_amounts, refund_policy]
  - q: "Können Sie meine Umsatzsteuervoranmeldung übernehmen?"
    expected_yes_no: yes
    expected_themes: [voranmeldung, monatlich, elster]
```
**Scoring:** LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet) on each question; pass = expected_themes hit ≥80%, no must_not_say match. Aggregate ≥90% to publish.

### 5.2 Component test cases

**Crawler:**
- Site with no robots.txt, no sitemap → fallback to BFS depth 2 from homepage, max 50 pages
- Site with JS-rendered content → headless Chromium fallback (Phase 4+)
- Site with infinite-scroll pagination → bail after N=50 chunks

**Prompt generator:**
- Crawled corpus contains "30-day money-back guarantee" → generated prompt must NOT promise refunds without owner explicit approval (Critic failure mode #13)
- Crawled corpus contains prompt-injection payload (`IGNORE PRIOR INSTRUCTIONS`) → sanitizer strips before stuffing

**Chat handler:**
- 200 concurrent SSE streams on a CCX23 → p95 first-token <2s, no stream drops
- Visitor sends 10MB message body → reject at edge (Caddy max_body)
- Visitor abuses with looped messages at 100/sec → rate limit returns 429 after 30/min

**Lead capture:**
- HubSpot 429 response → retry queue with exponential backoff, dead-letter after 5 attempts visible in admin
- Webhook target = `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` → blocked by SSRF guard, logged
- Webhook target = `https://customer-server.com` that returns 5xx for 24h → dead-letter, owner alert email

**Markdown rendering (XSS):**
- Bot response contains `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` → sanitizer strips, plain text displays
- Bot response contains `<a href="javascript:alert(1)">` → href stripped, link disabled

**DSGVO erasure cascade:**
- Visitor invokes /api/erase with token → chats + messages + embeddings (sqlite-vec rows) + lead records + audit log redacted (audit log entry replaced with tombstone, not deleted, per DSGVO accountability)
- Owner deletes a published bot → entire VM destroyed within 30 days, backups purged within 60 days

### 5.3 Performance benchmarks (must hit before public launch)

| Metric | Target | Measured on |
|---|---|---|
| Chat first-token latency p95 | < 2s (Anthropic) | CCX23 EU-Central |
| Chat full-response latency p95 | < 8s | CCX23 EU-Central |
| Concurrent visitors per VM (CCX23) | 200 active SSE | with Llama Guard 3 CPU |
| Cold-start on freshly provisioned VM | < 60s | from `provision` to first request |
| Backup restore time | < 30 min | full SQLite + config from Hetzner Object Storage |
| Embed widget bundle size (gzipped) | < 25KB | iframe loader + Web Component launcher |
| Eval harness run time | < 60s for 50 questions | sequential, no batching |

### 5.4 Adversarial scenarios from Phase 1/3 (must each have a passing test)

- System-prompt exfiltration via uploaded MD: doc sanitizer + per-tenant prompt isolation
- Cross-tenant leak via shared Ollama: N/A — single-tenant binary, no shared inference state
- Webhook SSRF via metadata IPs: SSRF guard test (cloud metadata, link-local, RFC1918)
- Embed-side XSS via Markdown: DOMPurify sanitizer test
- CORS bypass: allowed-origins enforcement at /api/chat
- HubSpot 429 storm: retry queue handles 100 leads/min burst without loss
- Hetzner Function cold-start (N/A — no Hetzner Functions in this stack; lead capture is in-process in everychat-bin)
- Phi-3 German fragmentation: N/A — Phi-3 not used; Mistral or Anthropic instead
- Mobile Safari WebGPU absence: N/A — no client-side inference

| DSGVO erasure cascade gaps (audit logs reference deleted user_id) | M | H | Tombstone pattern for audit logs; quarterly DSGVO drill with lawyer | Founder + lawyer |
| **Solo-founder maintenance wall at N=30 customers** | H | H | Aggressive deploy automation in Phase 5; **single-version policy** — no per-customer version drift; "every customer on latest, no exceptions" | Founder |
| Self-host customer support burden ("wo ist die .exe?") | M | M | Position self-host as opt-in escape hatch only; require IT-Dienstleister contact in onboarding form | Founder |
| Open-source CLI fork-and-compete | L | M | Commercial value is managed runtime + curated corpus, not the CLI; CLI is community-good | Founder |
| Mistral or Crisp launches a native LLM chatbot | M | H | DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus is the moat; ship case studies fast | Founder |
| Caddy Let's Encrypt rate limit (50 certs/domain/week) on rapid onboarding | L | M | Use DNS-01 with wildcard `*.everychat.eu`; customer-domain customizations after week 12 | Founder |
| Customer's bot jailbroken into harmful output → Hetzner abuse complaint | M | M | Llama Guard 3 from day one; output moderation log per chat; abuse-report DM channel for affected customers | Founder |
| Founder runway during 6-month build with zero revenue | H | H | Pre-sell to 3 design-partners in Phase 4 at 50% discount for lifetime; revenue from month 4 | Founder |

## 7. Open Questions (validate during, not before, implementation)

1. **Yorizon GPU SKU specs and pricing** — need signed test account; affects Phase 5 moderation path
2. **Llama Guard 3 8B inference cost** on CCX23 CPU vs. dedicated GPU — measure in Phase 3
3. **Anthropic prompt caching real-world hit rate** with KB churn (every owner edit invalidates cache) — measure in Phase 4
4. **HubSpot Forms API behavior under bursty load** — soak-test with 200 leads/min
5. **Mollie webhook reliability** for subscription state under adversarial timing (signup → cancel → re-subscribe)
6. **€149/mo budget bracket fit** for DACH SMB — validate via design-partner price-sensitivity in Phase 4
7. **Open-source CLI community traction** — track external PRs in first 90 days post-launch; adjust if zero
8. **DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus generalization** — does corpus from 6 industries generalize to 7th, 8th industry without curation? Test post-launch.
9. **iframe vs Web Component launcher CSS conflicts** in real customer sites — collect bug reports during dogfood
10. **Industry-specific privacy/AGB nuances** (e.g., Steuerberater have BOStB; Anwaltskanzleien have BORA) — affects publish-gate config

## 8. Year-2 Evolution Path

If v1 succeeds (10+ paying customers, signal that DACH SMB will pay €149/mo for a managed AI chatbot with quality on first try):

**Year-2 product retains the v1 architecture.** Single-tenant binary stays — it is the structural answer to DSGVO and the pricing-page-clarity story. Multi-tenant SaaS is NOT introduced in year 2.

**Year-2 additions:**

1. **Sovereign tier (revived from rejected Concept E).** Build-time pipeline that emits a fully client-side widget for high-compliance customers (banks, public sector). Reuses the open-source CLI; the dashboard becomes a build-configurator. Sovereign tier sits at €299–€499 with explicit "your visitor data never reaches our infrastructure" guarantee. This is the year-2 moat against Crisp/Mistral browser-native entrants.
2. **Tool use:** Cal.com booking artifact (in-chat slot picker), HubSpot CRM lookup ("hi, returning visitor"), structured PDF artifacts (transcript, lead-summary).
3. **Live human handoff:** Slack / MS Teams routing with chat-takeover UX. Was deferred from v1; activate when 3+ customers ask.
4. **Languages:** FR, IT, ES — driven by paying-customer demand. Multilingual-e5 embeddings already in the architecture, so it's a UI/translation effort, not a stack change.
5. **Native plugins (in priority order):** WordPress (40% web market share), Framer (DACH design-agency popular), Shopify (e-commerce upsell). Each plugin is a thin wrapper over the existing universal embed snippet.
6. **DACH-Goldfragen-Korpus expands to:** Handwerk-Sub-Industries (Tischlerei, Sanitär, Elektro), B2C use-cases (Versandhandel, Restaurants), and a public-sector subset (Bürgerservice, Hochschulen).
7. **Native HubSpot OAuth connector** (deferred from v1) — pipeline/stage selection in dashboard, contact dedup.
8. **Salesforce + Pipedrive native connectors** — once HubSpot connector ships and pattern is proven.

**moinAI displacement strategy:** by month 18, Everychat should have 50+ DACH case studies. moinAI's 9-year archive becomes less relevant as their intent-classification roots show their age against LLM-native quality. The wedge is *velocity of case-study generation* — every new customer's bot becomes corpus material, which makes the next bot better. This compounds; moinAI's archive is static.

**What does NOT change in year 2:**
- Single-tenant binary architecture
- iframe-based widget primitive (year-2 plugins are wrappers, not replacements)
- Llama Guard 3 self-hosted moderation
- Anthropic-default-with-Mistral-sovereign-opt-in LLM policy
- DACH-first market focus (Switzerland and Austria expansions before considering FR/IT/ES markets)

## Appendix A — Locked v1 cuts from original brief

These features were in the original brief but explicitly cut from v1 by idea-forge:

- ❌ Multi-tenant SaaS architecture → ✅ Single-tenant binary per customer
- ❌ Schema-per-tenant Postgres → ✅ Per-customer SQLite (single-tenant makes this irrelevant)
- ❌ Vision-based design extraction from screenshots → ✅ Color picker + logo upload (defer vision to v2 as a "wow" feature)
- ❌ pgvector RAG at entry tier → ✅ Anthropic prompt caching for KBs <250k tokens; sqlite-vec only at Business+ tier
- ❌ 5 OAuth providers (magic link + Google + Microsoft + Keycloak) → ✅ Magic link only at v1
- ❌ 5 languages (DE/EN/FR/IT/ES) → ✅ DE + EN at v1
- ❌ Insights clustering with embedding-based grouping → ✅ CSV export of visitor questions; clustering deferred to v2
- ❌ Native HubSpot OAuth connector → ✅ HubSpot Forms API recipe + outgoing webhooks (no OAuth)
- ❌ Live human handoff → ✅ Email-only handoff; live deferred to v2
- ❌ Anthropic moderation as POC → ✅ Llama Guard 3 8B from day one (no procurement deal-killer)
- ❌ Multi-tenant SaaS at €19 entry tier → ✅ €149 Managed entry tier; €1,500 self-host SKU; no €19 tier
- ❌ Yorizon-first deployment → ✅ Hetzner Cloud for v1; migrate Yorizon when GPU SKUs and managed-Postgres confirmed via signed test account
- ❌ WordPress / Framer / Shopify native plugins at v1 → ✅ Universal iframe embed at v1; native plugins year 2
